Jesus Christ, a servant, but not your servant, a savior, yes, but not a hero at your beck and
call that the servant of God who sets sinners free for the glory of God so that we may be
servants as well, tracing our lives over the life of Christ. Let's pray. Heavenly Father,
even when we think about Jesus, our thoughts so quickly turn to thinking about ourselves.
Even when we think about our salvation, our thoughts so quickly turn to ourselves and yet you call us to behold Jesus, to set our minds on Him, to consider Him in all of His glory.
And when we do, we are confronted with our own self-centeredness, our own desire to be in the spotlight of your attention.
Father, we pray that You would teach us to delight in Christ even as You do.
Rather than in ourselves, we pray that you would teach us to hope in Christ.
As you have set him forth as the hope of the world, we pray that our lives would be lives
that so clearly demonstrate that we have been brought into a relationship with you,
not because of who we are, but because of who he is.
And we pray this in Christ's name. Amen.
